correctness.rationale: Reconstruction: local L1 circle trace yields T_r f = anti-holomorphic derivative of disk average; D-prime convergence plus local uniform L1 gives iff derivative is measure by Riesz. The nonnegative kernel yields an exact upper variation bound and weak-star lower-semicontinuity gives its matching lower bound. Lebesgue differentiation gives a.e pointwise density, and subtracting the L1-approximated density leaves exactly singular variation. Explicit nested Cantor interval lengths have a strict two-child separation inequality and total cover length tending zero, and a two-parent interval mass estimate gives O(h log(1/h)^beta). The derivative is singular nonzero while circle integrals eventually vanish at almost every center. Analytic estimates justify all scales; checker only tests signs and finite identities.

The theorem gives an exact iff for measure-valued Cauchy–Riemann derivatives, quantitatively measures the singular information erased by a.e tests, and constructs examples with essentially Lipschitz-up-to-any-log regularity. This is a structural regularity boundary, not an arbitrary numerical slice or routine change of notation.
